title: Final: attributes and reflection
cards/0/q: Type t has one [Route] attribute. How many RouteAttribute objects does the loop create?
cards/0/explain: IsDefined looks at metadata and creates no object. GetCustomAttribute parses the blob and calls the constructor anew every time — 1000 calls, 1000 objects. Read once and cache.
cards/0/wrong/2: IsDefined does not call the constructor — it only checks that the row exists.
cards/1/q: Which line does not compile? The attribute constructor parameters match the argument types.
cards/1/explain: decimal is not on the list of attribute parameter types: CS0181. An enum, a string, nameof and a single-dimensional Type array are all allowed. Pass a fractional value as a double or a string.
cards/2/q: Which attributes does the compiler turn into flags and dedicated metadata tables rather than a CustomAttribute row? Select all.
cards/2/explain: Serializable is a bit in the type flags, DllImport is the ImplMap table, StructLayout is layout flags plus ClassLayout. The type loader reads them. Obsolete and Flags are ordinary attributes: the compiler and Enum.ToString read them.
cards/3/q: Put in order what happens inside t.GetCustomAttribute<RouteAttribute>()
cards/3/items/0: Find the CustomAttribute rows owned by t
cards/3/items/1: Keep those whose constructor belongs to RouteAttribute
cards/3/items/3: Call the constructor with the positional arguments
cards/3/items/4: Assign the named properties and fields
cards/3/explain: The object is built only at the very end and only on request. Until then the attribute is a table row and blob bytes.
cards/4/q: A hot loop calls a private method of someone else's type millions of times. The project targets .NET 8 and will later be published with Native AOT. What do you pick?
cards/4/explain: UnsafeAccessor costs as much as a direct call and needs no code generation at run time. Invoke is tens of nanoseconds and allocations on every call. A compiled expression is fast under the JIT but becomes an interpreter in Native AOT. dynamic does not see private methods.
cards/4/wrong/2: Under the JIT it is a good option, but in Native AOT Compile returns a delegate over an interpreter — slower than Invoke.
cards/5/q: Match the diagnostic code with its cause
cards/5/pairs/3/1: A Type passed without the required DynamicallyAccessedMembers annotation
cards/6/explain: For properties and events PropertyInfo.GetCustomAttributes ignores the inherit parameter and looks only at the override itself. The static Attribute.GetCustomAttributes walks the chain and finds [Track] on Base.Qty.
cards/7/q: In version 2 of the library the enum became enum Level { Low, Mid, High }. An app with [Priority(Level.High)], built against version 1 (Low, High), was not rebuilt. What does the attribute read?
cards/7/options/2: An exception when reading the attribute
cards/7/explain: The blob holds the number 1 — the value of High in version 1, not the name. On read that number becomes a Level from the new library, where 1 is Mid. Add new enum members at the end, or better, give values explicitly.
